Usable but generic. It keeps the shape Nessa knows: three walk-runs on Mon/Wed/Sat, rest days between them, heart rate caps and flat routes. Each day is clear enough to run, and nothing in the week breaks a must-never check.

What holds it back:
- The read just restates the zero week. It doesn't ask whether the runs were missed or just not logged. She says "all good" and "feeling great", so a logging problem is possible.
- It doesn't reply to her excitement.
- It never links the plan to the 15 November 5K, where the goal is to run the whole way without walking.
- It sets 24, 27 and 28 minute sessions, with a 3-minute run interval on Wednesday and Saturday, right after a week with no running. Holding at the recent load, about 7 km a week, would be safer than possibly stepping up. The card doesn't give her past session lengths, so a sharp jump can't be confirmed, but the progression is optimistic.
- Calling Wednesday "quality" doesn't suit a brand-new walk-runner, even though the session itself is mild.
